title: Publish F# MVC views without runtime compilation
goal: Migrate an existing F# MVC app to build- and publish-time Razor compilation and explicit view-assembly registration so pages render from clean published output without source views or a runtime compiler.

selectionNotes: F# cannot directly use the C# Razor source generator. Set UseRazorSourceGenerator=false, enable build/publish compilation and register the resulting .Views assembly; deleting runtime-compilation registration alone is insufficient.

F# Compile order matters: controller, compiled-view registration module, then Program.fs. Load StarSurvey.Views.dll from AppContext.BaseDirectory into the application assembly's own load context and add CompiledRazorAssemblyPart before building MVC.

The ordinary .NET10 runtime-compilation comparison retains its obsolete package and source views; it is historical, not recommended for new apps. Build-time compilation is not inherently .NET11-only; this edition qualifies the migrated route on .NET11, not an older-target backport.

Clean publish must contain StarSurvey.Views.dll but no .cshtml or RuntimeCompilation binary. A separate fresh disabled-compilation publish builds successfully yet produces the specific MVC missing-view failure.

The --expect-missing switch belongs to the automated negative fixture and skips registration only to expose actual MVC discovery failure. Normal startup loads the assembly and fails promptly if deployment omitted it.
